sponsors: Reps. George Rauscher, Mia Costello, Ky Holland
party: Republican (Rauscher, Costello); Nonpartisan/independent (Holland, per Ballotpedia; runs in Alaska's nonpartisan primary system for District 9)
status: (H) FIN; status date 2025-04-11 (no further action recorded through 2026-07-31)
key_provisions: Not a moratorium. Would establish a Joint Legislative Task Force on Artificial Intelligence. The proposal is relevant because it covers AI development and policy risks, but it does not impose siting, utility, or permitting restrictions on data centers.

sponsors: Sen. Bryan King; Rep. Ron McNair
status: All Senate resolutions (SR7-SR12) failed third-reading floor votes 2026-04-21 and formally died at Sine Die adjournment 2026-04-29; all House resolutions (HR1010-HR1015) died in House Rules Committee at Sine Die adjournment 2026-04-29. Underlying nonappropriation bills were never authorized for introduction.
key_provisions: Sought authorization to introduce nonappropriation bills on crypto-mining local control, extraordinary electricity-use fees, foreign hardware/software restrictions, money-transmitter licensing, six-month advance notice before land acquisition or construction, and water-use monitoring.

sponsors: Same House sponsor group as HR196
status: House adopted 2026-04-09; transmitted to Senate; Senate adopted as amended (SD1) 2026-04-27; returned to and adopted in final form by the House same day - fully adopted by both chambers
key_provisions: Concurrent-resolution version of the large-data-center working group request. The HD1 text uses the same 5 MW threshold and study scope as HR196.

sponsors: Reps. Nicole Lowen, Terez Amato, Della Au Belatti, Tina Grandinetti, Jeanne Kapela, Sue Keohokapu-Lee Loy, Matthias Kusch, Lisa Marten, Tyson Miyake, Amy Perruso, Mahina Poepoe, Shirley Ann Templo, Chris Todd
status: Adopted by the House in final form 2026-04-09 (House-only resolution; no Senate action required)
key_provisions: Requests the Hawaii State Energy Office to convene a working group to study data centers requiring 5 MW or more in instantaneous demand. Topics include utility impacts, ratepayer protection, water use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy alignment, and grid reliability.

sponsors: Sen. Glenn Wakai and Senate co-sponsors including Angus McKelvey, Brandon Elefante, Carol Fukunaga, Tim Richards, Jarrett Keohokalole, Joy San Buenaventura, Karl Rhoads, and Stanley Chang
party: D (all listed Senate co-sponsors caucus as Democrats; Hawaii Senate has had no Republican members since 2024)
status: SR90 (Senate-only resolution): adopted by the Senate as amended (SD1) 2026-04-09, certified copies sent 2026-05-12 - final action, fully adopted. SCR95 (companion Senate Concurrent Resolution): passed Senate as amended (SD1) 2026-04-09, transmitted to and received by the House the same day, referred to House EEP/FIN 2026-04-10; no further House action recorded - died in House committee, never adopted by the second chamber
key_provisions: Senate measures requesting a Hawaii State Energy Office working group on large data centers, including possible reporting, water-impact assessment, and safeguards for ratepayers and grid reliability.

status: Adopted by House 93-0 on 2025-06-08; received by Senate same day but never brought up for concurrence -- returned to Senate calendar subject to call 2025-06-09 and died there when the 2025 RS ended
key_provisions: Would create a special task force to study interagency consultation for data centers and natural resource planning, including water and energy impacts.

status: Passed House 2025-04-16; tabled in Senate committee 2025-04-24; died in standing committee 2025-05-22
key_provisions: Would have requested an interim study of data center impacts on grid adequacy, electric rates, stranded utility investment, water demand, affordability, and regulatory safeguards. Not a moratorium bill.

sponsors: Sen. Bob Smith; Sen. Linda Greenstein
status: Reported from Senate Environment and Energy Committee 2026-03-16; resolution passed by the full Senate 2026-03-23 (22-15) and filed with the Secretary of State 2026-03-23
key_provisions: Urges PJM-region states and the District of Columbia to adopt policies requiring data centers to obtain electricity from new zero- or low-emission sources.

sponsors: Rep. Paul Friel; Rep. Kyle Donahue; Rep. Kyle Mullins; Rep. Chris Pielli
status: Legacy precursor memo linked by the official memo page to HB 2496. The associated bill passed the House on 2026-06-24 and was reported amended with first consideration in the Senate on 2026-06-30. These are the bill's procedural events, not a second passage of the memo.
key_provisions: Pre-introduction memo proposing time for municipalities to develop data-center zoning rules; its official page links to HB 2496. The associated bill, separately retained as pa-hb2496, now contains the PN 3727 optional new-application pause with duration, earlier-application and repeat-use limits. This precursor row is not an additional independent bill.

status: Legacy precursor memo linked by its official page to SB 1345. The associated bill's history records re-referral to Senate Rules and Executive Nominations on 2026-09-30 after earlier committee and consideration events. The prior record reports a 2-9 vote concerning proposed SB 1359 language; that vote and its procedural description remain unverified here.
key_provisions: Pre-introduction memo proposing municipal authority to consider a temporary data-center moratorium; its official page links to SB 1345. The separately retained bill row pa-sb1345 describes the later PN 1889 resolution, maximum term and exceptions. This precursor is not an additional independent bill or an adopted municipal pause.

status: Legacy precursor memo linked by its official page to SB 1359, whose history lists referral to Senate Local Government on 2026-06-04. The separate claim about SB 1359 language offered as an amendment to another bill is not direct passage or failure of this bill and remains unverified here.
key_provisions: Pre-introduction memo proposing a three-year statewide hyperscale-data-center development moratorium, including described supporting infrastructure. The official page links to SB 1359, separately retained as pa-sb1359. This precursor proposal is not an additional independent bill or enacted statewide moratorium.

status: Referred to Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee 2025-11-05; not adopted/agreed to by the Senate through 2026-07-31.
key_provisions: Directs Joint State Government Commission, PUC, DCED, and DEP to assess and recommend a comprehensive state energy strategy, including high-energy-use sectors such as data centers.

status: Referred to Senate Local Government 2025-03-25; no further action recorded before 89R sine die 2025-06-02 - resolution died in committee, never adopted by either chamber and never submitted to voters.
